summary.text: A caldera is a large cauldron-shaped hollow that forms soon after a volcanic eruption empties a magma chamber.
With the magma gone, the chamber cannot hold up the rock above, so the ground collapses into it, leaving a depression that may be dozens of kilometres across.
Because it forms by sinking and collapse rather than by an explosion or impact, a caldera is really a kind of sinkhole, not a crater.

facts.label: Most recent collapses
facts.value: Kīlauea in 2018, Hunga Tonga–Hunga Haʻapai in 2022

facts.label: Collapse area
facts.value: May reach hundreds of square kilometres

items.prompt: A tour guide calls a vast volcanic hollow "a crater blasted out by an explosion". What is it more accurately?
items.explain: A caldera forms through subsidence and collapse, not an explosion or impact, so it is a type of sinkhole.

items.prompt: What sets up the collapse that forms a caldera?

options.label: Lava piling up on the summit

items.explain: Collapse is triggered when the magma chamber beneath the volcano empties and can no longer support the weight above.

items.prompt: Thousands of volcanic eruptions happen each century. How many caldera-forming collapses are known between 1911 and 2022?
items.explain: Caldera formation is rare: only nine collapses are known in that period.

items.prompt: After a caldera forms, fresh magma keeps flowing into the collapsed chamber below. What can happen to the caldera's center?

options.label: It is pushed up into a dome

items.explain: Continued injection of magma can uplift the center as a resurgent dome, as seen at Yellowstone and Lake Toba.

items.prompt: Thick, silica-rich magma rises toward the surface. What makes it burst apart into ash?

options.label: It cools and cracks into dust
Its gases bubble out as pressure drops
It catches fire on meeting air
Friction with the rock grinds it

items.explain: Near the surface the drop in pressure makes dissolved gases rapidly bubble out, fragmenting the magma into ash and tephra.

items.prompt: Why might a mining company explore an ancient, worn-down caldera?

options.label: Its ash layers hold large oil pools
Its floor is rich in coal seams
Hot fluids may have left metal ores

items.explain: Metal-rich fluids can circulate through a caldera, forming ore deposits of lead, silver, gold, mercury, lithium and uranium.
